summary: Backend-only smoke test of the new task/check-in recurrence feature. 15/17 tests passed. Two failures: (1) POST /api/tasks/{id}/recurrence/generate is NOT idempotent by due_date — calling twice creates duplicate sibling tasks on the same date, violating spec §5; (2) missing 'cadence' field returns 422 (Pydantic default) instead of 400 as spec §11 requires. All other recurrence semantics (auto-spawn on completion, pre-generate, end_type=until/count, extended goal cadences, alternate_day period membership in /checkins/required, legacy daily cadence) work correctly.

critical.issue: Not idempotent by due_date. Calling twice with count=3 creates 6 sibling tasks — 3 duplicates on the exact same due_dates (2026-09-08, 2026-09-15, 2026-09-22). Root cause: _pre_generate_series in server.py L1381-1436 does not check for an existing sibling with the same series_id + due_date before insert_one. Contrast with _maybe_spawn_next_occurrence (L1454-1466) which does perform this check. Fix: inside the loop in _pre_generate_series, before insert, query db.tasks.find_one({user_id, series_id, due_date=next_due}) and skip if it exists (also advance cursor_due and continue).

minor.issue: Returns 422 (Pydantic validation) instead of 400. Root cause: TaskRecurrenceSpec pydantic model declares 'cadence: str' as required, so Pydantic rejects the payload before HTTPException(status_code=400) in create_task can run. All other invalid-recurrence cases (unknown cadence, until without end_date, count=0, end_date<anchor) correctly return 400 from normalise_recurrence. Fix: either make cadence Optional[str] on TaskRecurrenceSpec (letting normalise_recurrence raise the 400) or add a Pydantic validator that converts to a 400 in the endpoint. Alternatively, update the spec to accept 422 for schema-level violations.

action_items: Fix _pre_generate_series idempotency by adding a per-iteration due_date existence check within the same series_id before inserting the child task (critical, blocks the spec for /recurrence/generate).
Decide whether 'missing cadence' should return 400 or 422; if 400 is required, make cadence Optional[str] on TaskRecurrenceSpec so normalise_recurrence produces the HTTPException(400).

rca_of_issue: Issue 1 (idempotency): _pre_generate_series is invoked by three call sites — task creation with pre_generate_count>0, POST /tasks/{id}/recurrence with pre_generate_count>0, and POST /tasks/{id}/recurrence/generate. Only the third call site is meant to be user-triggered repeatedly. Since the helper never queries for an existing sibling with the same (user_id, series_id, due_date), subsequent invocations always append duplicates. Reproduction: create task with weekly recurrence pre_generate_count=0 → POST /recurrence/generate {count:3} → POST /recurrence/generate {count:3} again → observe 6 sibling tasks with only 3 distinct due_dates. Mitigation: inside the loop, add `if await db.tasks.find_one({"user_id": base_task["user_id"], "series_id": base_task["series_id"], "due_date": next_due}, {"_id":0, "id":1}): cursor_due = next_due; continue`. Issue 2 (422 vs 400): FastAPI/Pydantic returns 422 for Request-body schema violations before any endpoint code runs. To honour the spec's 400, drop the required-ness from the model for `cadence` (make Optional[str]) so the body deserialises and normalise_recurrence raises the friendly ValueError converted to 400.
